name: Pontius Pilate
bio: Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea, questioned Jesus and found no answer when accused by the chief priests. Recognizing the charges were driven by envy and warned by his wife's troubled dream, Pilate offered the crowd a choice between releasing Jesus or the notorious prisoner Barabbas; persuaded by the chief priests, the crowd demanded Barabbas's release and Jesus's crucifixion. Unable to quell the mob, Pilate symbolically washed his hands of responsibility for Jesus's blood, then had him scourged and handed over for crucifixion. He later granted Joseph of Arimathea's request for Jesus's body, and agreed to have the tomb secured and guarded at the chief priests' request (Matthew 27:1-66).
